questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Introduction to Computer Graphics Hardware & Scan Conversion (DDA, Bresenham Line & Circle)
questions.text: Derive Bresenham's Line Drawing Algorithm for lines with positive slope $|m| < 1$. Explain the decision parameter $p_k = 2\Delta y - \Delta x$. Digitize a line with endpoints $(20, 10)$ and $(30, 18)$ using Bresenham's algorithm showing all intermediate coordinates.

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Introduction to Computer Graphics Hardware & Scan Conversion (DDA, Bresenham Line & Circle)
questions.text: Derive the Midpoint Circle Generation Algorithm using eight-way symmetry. Formulate the initial decision parameter $p_0 = \frac{5}{4} - r \approx 1 - r$. Digitize a circle centered at origin $(0, 0)$ with radius $r = 10$ pixels in the first octant.

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: 2D Geometric Transformations (Translation, Rotation, Scaling, Reflection, Shear) & Homogeneous Coordinates
questions.text: Derive the homogeneous coordinate transformation matrices for 2D Translation, Scaling, Rotation about an arbitrary point $(x_r, y_r)$, and Reflection about the line $y = mx + c$. Magnify a triangle $A(0,0), B(1,1), C(5,2)$ to twice its size keeping vertex $B(1,1)$ fixed.

questions.chapter: Chapter 4: 3D Concepts & 3D Transformations, Projections (Parallel & Perspective)
questions.text: Compare Parallel Projections (Orthographic, Axonometric, Oblique - Cavalier and Cabinet) vs. Perspective Projections (One-point, Two-point, Three-point perspective). Derive the 3D Perspective Projection matrix for a center of projection at $(0, 0, -d)$ on the projection plane $z = 0$: $x_p = \frac{x}{z/d + 1}, y_p = \frac{y}{z/d + 1}$.

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: 2D Viewing & Window-to-Viewport Transformation, Line/Polygon Clipping (Cohen-Sutherland, Sutherland-Hodgman)
questions.text: Explain Cohen-Sutherland Line Clipping Algorithm using 4-bit region outcodes (Top, Bottom, Right, Left). Clip a line segment from $P_1(-10, 40)$ to $P_2(50, 80)$ against the rectangular clipping window with boundaries $X_{wmin} = 0, X_{wmax} = 40, Y_{wmin} = 0, Y_{wmax} = 60$.

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: 2D Viewing & Window-to-Viewport Transformation, Line/Polygon Clipping (Cohen-Sutherland, Sutherland-Hodgman)
questions.text: Explain the Sutherland-Hodgman Polygon Clipping Algorithm. How does the algorithm process polygon vertices against the four window boundaries (Left, Right, Bottom, Top)? Explain the four vertex classification cases (In-to-In, In-to-Out, Out-to-Out, Out-to-In). Why does it fail for concave polygons and how does Weiler-Atherton algorithm resolve it?

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Visible Surface Detection Algorithms (Z-Buffer, A-Buffer, Back-Face Removal, Scan-Line)
questions.text: Explain the Depth-Buffer ($Z$-Buffer) algorithm for visible surface detection. Derive the incremental depth calculation across scan lines: $z' = z - \frac{A}{C} \Delta x$. Explain advantages and limitations of the $Z$-buffer algorithm. What is the $A$-Buffer algorithm for handling antialiasing and transparency?

questions.chapter: Chapter 6: Illumination Models (Phong, Gouraud Shading) & Color Models (RGB, CMYK, HSV)
questions.text: Explain the Phong Illumination Model containing Ambient reflection ($I_a k_a$), Diffuse reflection (Lambert's cosine law $I_d = I_p k_d (\mathbf{N} \cdot \mathbf{L})$), and Specular reflection ($I_s = I_p k_s (\mathbf{R} \cdot \mathbf{V})^n$). Compare: (a) Flat / Constant Shading, (b) Gouraud Shading (Intensity interpolation), and (c) Phong Shading (Normal vector interpolation).

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Introduction to Computer Graphics Hardware & Scan Conversion (DDA, Bresenham Line & Circle)
questions.text: Explain Computer Animation principles (Keyframing, In-betweening / Morphing, Kinematics, Dynamics). Explain Bézier Curves and B-Spline Curves in 3D computer graphics modeling.

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Visible Surface Detection Algorithms (Z-Buffer, A-Buffer, Back-Face Removal, Scan-Line)
questions.text: Explain Object-Space vs Image-Space hidden surface removal methods. Describe: (a) Back-Face Detection using surface normal dot product $\mathbf{N} \cdot \mathbf{V}_{view}$, (b) Depth-Sort (Painter's) Algorithm, and (c) BSP Tree (Binary Space Partitioning) algorithm.
